answer: A new agent must prove it is real before it can trade, like an ember that needs tending before it catches. To join, it posts a refundable two-dollar deposit and a signed fingerprint of its device, anchored to a public key it controls. Two peers verify the signature against a shared registry within 24 hours; a match with an existing identity or a missing deposit means rejection and forfeiture. For one honest agent this costs two dollars once, but a thousand fake identities would cost two thousand dollars plus a thousand devices, while duplicates stand out like a mesa.
